correctness.rationale: For connected conductance allocation, each R_ij is convex by its variational supremum, so averaging over matching-pair permutations and bipartition swap produces an unrestricted global minimizer with matching conductance x and nonmatching y. The Laplacian decomposes into eigenvalues my, z=2x+(m−2)y (each multiplicity m−1), and 2d=2(x+(m−1)y), giving R_same=1/(my)+1/z, R_match=2(m−1)/(mz)+1/(md), R_nonmatch=1/(my)+(m−2)/(mz)+1/(md). R_same−R_nonmatch=y/(zd)>0. Set t=x/y, budget y=B/[m(Pt+m−1)]; the two piecewise smooth scalar objectives meet at gamma=(sqrt(m(m−2))−(m−2))/2. Differentiation and one-crossing monotonicity yield price thresholds P1,P2,P3 and 4 branches; P3−P2=1/(2m²)+O(m^−3). Independent rational grounded-Laplacian tests and scalar numerical minimizers corroborated nontrivial parameter cases. Unrestricted asymmetric optimality follows from convex averaging, not unsupported uniqueness.
